bodies.name: Io
bodies.nativeSurface: Own-body NASA3D Galileo/Voyager mosaic preserved. Unchanged JIRAM2024 infrared publisher still and Galileo1999/JunoSRU2023 comparison provide measured context, not calibrated visible albedo. Mosaic frame, coverage, source association and photometric registration remain open.
measured: Juno JIRAM observed strong southern-hemisphere infrared emission2024-12-27; saturation and missing field of view remain instrument limits, not surface colours or gaps.
Juno SRU observed2023-12-30 night-side thermal glow near South Zal Mons under Jupiter-shine. Comparison Galileo panel is circa1999, exact day unverified.
Catalogue radius1821.6km and semimajor axis421800km preserved. Sulfur dioxide dominates Io's tenuous atmosphere; its surface includes volcanic deposits and SO2 frost.
modelled: Mura et al.2026 first published2026-01-10 interpret synchronized activity as possible regional reservoir connections, not directly imaged plumbing. Deep magma ocean not ruled out; a shallow global molten layer is disfavoured by referenced tidal-response modelling.
Representative Sun geometry at5.2044AU via skyGeometry, nominal90degree HFOV, Sun outside frame.
Spherical Jupiter69911km radius at assumed observer distance421800−1821.6km gives19.164505degrees via skyGeometry; geometry guide only, no dated registration.
assumed: Invented local pale sulfur-associated deposits, charcoal cooled silicate lava, rocks, cracks and a small glowing fissure. Fractions, visible colours, lava temperature and eruption state unmeasured; no mapped named locality.

Jupiter-facing hypothetical observer with independently invented cloud bands, phase, orientation, reflected light and exposure; no observed Jupiter map reused. Tenuous atmosphere represented by black sky without Earthlike haze.
unknown: Local chemistry, rock/grain placement, lava crust age, radiometry, scene registration and actual spectral transfer remain unverified.
Reservoir topology and global melt geometry remain hypotheses; local connections do not establish a globally molten ocean. No survivable landing claim.
No verified live Io-specific scientific stream; recent mission images assessed without an exhaustive newest-observation claim.

prompts.surface: Create one independent hypothetical LOCAL SURFACE OF IO scientific observer illustration, wide16:9 without text. Low camera above very cold muted sulfur-yellow and cream frost/deposit plains with dark charcoal cooled fractured silicate lava patches, shallow irregular volcanic depression in middle distance and a small localized dull orange-red fresh lava fissure. Sparse low rocky fragments, broad low-relief solid terrain. The local site, material distribution, stones, cracks, visible colour and volcanic phase are invented, not mapped measured Io geography. Thin SO2 atmosphere is too tenuous for an Earthlike sky: overhead black space, no fog, no clouds, no blue atmosphere, no thick smoke. Direct sunlight with hard shadows, restrained exposure, most ground cold and unglowing; no global magma sea or all-over orange lava. Do not copy, recolour or trace any observed Moon, Mars, Venus, Io or other map/photo. No terrestrial volcano cone, water, vegetation, people, lander or habitability claim. Jupiter and Sun outside frame. This is independently imagined terrain guided by volcanism/sulfur-deposit concepts, not an observed photograph or exact named patera. Smooth enough for compact preview; no dramatic plume.

Jupiter-facing hemisphere, black space above (Io's tenuous SO2 does not make a thick Earthlike atmosphere). Jupiter disc has independently invented broad pale cream/tan/cloud bands, subtle turbulent variations, no recognizable copied Jupiter map, no pasted/recoloured observed imagery or Great Red Spot registration. Slight gibbous shading; phase, orientation and exposure imaginary and not dated. Sun outside frame. Restrained Jupiter-shine on foreground shadows, no fog/blue atmosphere/dense star clutter, no other giant moons. No water, plants, people, spacecraft or survivable landing claim. Terrain/cracks/material fractions/colour and cloud morphology invented; no analog skins or observedMoon/Mars/Jupiter map reuse. No globally molten ground, no all-over lava glow. Keep Jupiter modest, about16.88percent canvas width rather than dominating sky. Smooth detail suited to compact app preview.
